translations.text: In this deed God's might is shown, and his humility.
The law of Moses forbade anyone to touch a leper, but the humble Christ would not despise him, though he was loathsome, and he also showed that he was Lord of the old law, and not its servant.
Truly, God's command is deed, just as the psalmist said, "He spoke it, and the creatures were made. He commanded, and they were created."
In the spiritual sense this leprous man signified all mankind, which was loathsomely leprous with various sins in the inner man;
We must rightly believe in Christ, that he can heal our souls of the stains of sin; and we must steadfastly ask that his will be done.
His hand signifies his might and his incarnation. Just as Christ healed the leper by the touch of his hand, so too he redeemed us from the sins of our souls by taking on our flesh;
just as the prophet Isaiah said, "Truly he himself took away our sicknesses, and he himself bore our sorrows."
When he forbade the healed leper to make it known to anyone, by that he gave us an example that we should not spread abroad our good deeds,
but we must shun vain boasting with our inmost heart, if we do some little thing for good.

So too must the one who is inwardly leprous with deadly sins come to God's priest, and reveal his secret to the spiritual physician, and, by his counsel and help, heal his soul's wounds by doing penance.

So must the spiritual priest do: he must correct God's people, and cut off and excommunicate from Christian people the one who is so leprous in wicked habits that he defiles others with his wickedness;
I tell you truly, that many will come from the east and from the west, and will rest with Abraham the patriarch, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
Then he asked at what hour he had grown better. They said, "Yesterday, past midday, the fever left him."
Then the father realized that it was the hour in which the Saviour had said to him, "Go home; your son lives." The king then believed in God, and all his household."
The Lord would not, when invited, go in bodily form to the king's sick child, but healed him while absent, by his word; yet he was ready, uninvited, to go in bodily form with the centurion.

Everyone knows well that a king has greater power than any centurion, but the Almighty Son of God showed by that deed that we should not honour the powerful for their power, but for their human nature;
nor should we despise the poor for their poverty; rather we should honour God's image in them.
The humble Son of God was ready to visit the servant in person, and he healed the nobleman by a command;
Of this the prophet said, "The Lord on high looks upon the humble, and knows the proud from afar."

The Lord marvelled at the centurion's faith, not as though he had not known him before, he who knows all things; but he made the man's faith known to people by praising it, since it was wonderful to him.

Where did that faith come to the officer from, except from the grace of Christ, who afterwards praised him with these words? "Truly I say to you, I have not found such great faith in the nation of Israel."
This was not said of the patriarchs or prophets, but of the people then present, who were not yet of such great faith.
Mary and Martha were two sisters who believed very greatly in God: they said to Christ, "Lord, if you had been here, our brother would not have died."
This officer said to Christ, "Speak your word, and my servant will be healed. I am a man set under authority, having soldiers under me;
and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; to another, Come, and he comes; to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
How much more can you, who are Almighty God, accomplish by your command whatever you will!"
The Lord said, "I say to you in truth, that many will come from the east and from the west, and will rest with Abraham the patriarch, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

These words are pleasant to hear, and they greatly gladden our hearts: that many will come from the east of the world, and from the west, to the kingdom of heaven, and will reign with the patriarchs in everlasting joy.

By the two regions, east and west, are signified the four corners of the whole world, from which God's chosen ones of every nation will be gathered to the dwelling of the patriarchs and of all the saints.
By the east may be signified those who turn to God in youth; because in the east is the beginning of the day.
By the west are signified those who turn to God's service in old age, because the day ends in the west.
This following saying is very fearful: "The children of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
The children of the kingdom are the Jews, over whom God reigned through the old law; but they rejected Christ and despised his teaching;
and he will cast them into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Many rich men, however, thrive with God, if they are righteous and merciful.

The patriarch Abraham was a rich man, and David the great king, and Zacchaeus, who gave half his possessions to the poor, and with the other half repaid fourfold whatever he had previously taken wrongfully, single for single.
These rich men and those like them come, through good conversion, to the eternal kingdom, which will never fail them.
Those are called children of God who love him more than this world;
and those are called the children of the kingdom who plant the roots of their hearts in this present life more than in Christ: such will be cast into darkness.
